source_caption:
The Intouchables (2011) is one of those movies that can make you laugh and hit you right in the heart.

After becoming quadriplegic following a paragliding accident, wealthy businessman Philippe hires Driss, a young man from the Paris suburbs with no experience as a caregiver. What starts as an unlikely working relationship slowly turns into a genuine friendship.

François Cluzet and Omar Sy are the heart of the movie. Their chemistry feels so effortless, and the film never lets Philippe be defined only by his disability. There’s humor, warmth, great music, and plenty of moments that stay with you.

What makes it even more special is that the story was inspired by a real friendship between Philippe Pozzo di Borgo and Abdel Sellou. The filmmakers changed some details for the movie, including Driss’ nationality, and specifically wanted Omar Sy for the role. Sy went on to win the César Award for Best Actor for his performance. 

And somehow, a relatively small French film became a worldwide hit, earning more than $426 million globally. 

If you haven’t seen it yet, this one is absolutely worth your time.

source_details.title: The Intouchables
source_details.synopsis: The Intouchables (French: Intouchables, pronounced [ɛ̃tuʃablə]), also known as Untouchable in the UK, Ireland, and Scandinavia, and 1+1 in Eastern Europe, is a 2011 French buddy comedy-drama film written and directed by Éric Toledano and Olivier Nakache. It stars François Cluzet and Omar Sy. The plot of the film is inspired by the true story of Philippe Pozzo di Borgo and his French-Algerian carer Abdel Sellou, discovered by the directors in À la vie, à la mort, a documentary film. Nine weeks after its release in France on 2 November 2011, it became the second highest-grossing French film in France, after the 2008 film Welcome to the Sticks.
